memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I said I would scatter them and erase their name from human memory, but I dreaded the taunt of the enemy, lest the adversary misunderstand and say, "Our hand has triumphed; the Lord has not done all this."' They are a nation without sense, there is no discernment in them. If only they were wise and would understand this and discern what their end will be!" — Deut 32:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we see something wonderful even in the midst of judgment — God's restraining mercy. He says He could have scattered His people entirely and erased their memory, yet He held back. For the sake of His own name and glory, He restrained the full weight of what their sin deserved. God's mercy limits His judgment. Even when His people deserve to be utterly consumed, He shows restraint.

This tells us so much about God's heart. He is "slow to anger" (Psa 103:8), not quick to give us what our sin deserves. How often has God held back consequences we could not see, shown patience we did not earn, and given us time to turn back? His restraining mercy surrounds us constantly, mostly unnoticed.

Then comes a heartfelt cry: "If only they were wise and would understand... discern what their end will be!" You can hear the longing in it — God wishing His people would simply grasp the path they are on and turn back before it is too late. This is the yearning of a God who "does not want anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance" (2 Pet 3:9).

That longing was answered in Christ, who wept over Jerusalem, longing to gather His people (Luke 19:41-42). The God who restrains judgment and yearns for our understanding has come near in Jesus to save us. So respond to His patience. Do not presume on His restraint, but let His mercy lead you to repentance and wisdom today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God shown me restraining mercy I did not deserve?
2. Am I responding to God's patience, or presuming on it?
3. What would it mean to be truly "wise" about the path I am on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Merciful God, thank You for restraining judgment and showing patience I have not earned. Do not let me presume on Your mercy, but let it lead me to repentance and wisdom. Draw me close before it is too late. Amen.
